title: Fixed Crosshatched Roller and Bent Neck Texturing Tool
description: One newly authored complete static printmaking-roulette-inspired tool. One small broad cylindrical drum has real integral coarse diamond-like relief formed by two crossing families of recessed diagonal grooves around its whole circumference, full annular end walls and a genuine through axle bore. A single continuous bent metal-look neck becomes the transverse axle, enters a whole pear-shaped long wooden grip and carries a complete retaining end cap; one full annular collar covers the grip root. The entire grip rests on its original finite lower facet while the textured head remains slightly raised. Every profile, groove field, neck bend and coordinate is new, not an old paint-roller sleeve reduced in size or a brayer fork removed. Unlike those plain long coating rollers, the characteristic component here is an integral deeply relieved short cylindrical texturing drum; it is not a thin toothed tracing/pounce disc or a broad serrated rocker plate. Five closed editable bodies, four constant opaque PBR roles, metres native Z up, one model zero scenes. Generic category appearance only, no maker marks or copied dimensions. Coarse relief is a visual convention, not a usable tooth grade; static small shaft/bore overlaps are intentional attachment, not rotating bearing clearance. No paper, ink, metal plate, actual rolling, engraving, scoring, pressure, print result, tooling sharpness, manufacturing, ergonomic or safety capability made or verified. No rig, animation or interaction.
